claims.statement: Job ID uniquely keys a job configuration map within jobs; starts with letter or underscore and contains only alphanumerics, hyphens or underscores. Display names in the two-job example are distinct from job identifiers.
Job name is the UI display name, not the unique job ID or native execution receipt.

needs is string or array of job IDs requiring successful dependencies; failure/skip propagates down the dependency chain unless a conditional permits continuation. Example job1→job2→job3 also has job3 directly require both predecessors.
always() permits dependent job3 after both dependencies complete regardless of success; it does not turn failed predecessors into passing evidence or authorize bypassing acceptance gates.

Jobs default parallel and each has runs-on environment; needs imposes ordering. Unlimited job wording is explicitly bounded by workflow usage limits, not unlimited concurrency/cost. API exposes run-job unique IDs separately.
Example job defaults set Bash and ./scripts on ubuntu-latest. Values are illustrative; directory existence and executed shell behavior remain unverified.

Job defaults.run supplies shell/working-directory for its run steps, with workflow-level counterpart and specificity include. Source calls out overrides at job defaults.run and steps[*].run; that wording requires reconciliation with actual shell/working-directory step keys, not blindly adopted.

Job defaults is a map of job-step default settings, with workflow defaults and more-specific override reusable referenced; source description does not establish arbitrary defaults accepted for every step type.
shell selects a step shell and includes reusable-keyword, supported-shells and default precedence fragments. Those dependency bodies/rendering remain separately reviewed.
working-directory selects shell step working directory; existence and precedence come from separate includes. Fragment alone does not prove directory availability.

Workflow defaults.run sets shell and working-directory for run steps, with per-job counterpart; contexts and expressions are prohibited at this keyword. Example uses Bash and ./scripts, not universal target settings.
Workflow defaults is a map applying defaults across jobs, with per-job alternatives and specificity include; actual valid default keys require parent/schema review.

Workflow example sets permissions: read-all for all jobs. Prose 'all permissions read' must be qualified by scopes without read capability, especially previously reviewed id-token write/none; not unconditional literal read support or recommended blanket permissions.

Stale-job example grants issues and pull-requests write, all other permissions none, and includes action-stale. This is job-specific illustrative privilege, not adopted automatic issue closure or reviewed action implementation.
Larger-runner names can determine function; code-scanning default setup requires code-scanning name in this source. Renaming is not authorized and linked configuration remains separate.
Larger runners are described for organizations/enterprises on Team or GHE Cloud; availability statement does not prove target entitlement or provisioning.
Using more than ten static-IP larger-runner pools requires contacting support according to pinned guidance; this is not immutable technical ceiling or actual approved expansion.

Pinned macOS Large Intel row gives 12 CPUs,30GB RAM,14GB SSD and latest/14/15/26 large labels, marking15 latest. XLarge M2 arm64 row gives5 CPUs plus8 GPU acceleration,14GB RAM/SSD and latest/14/15/26 plus preview xcode27 xlarge labels. Preserve dimensions and source date, not current inventory or benchmark proof.
YAML learning fragment links an external primer; navigation is reference-only, not full primer review or verified workflow validity.

Attestations are useful when tied to consumed artifacts; source recommends deleting accidental, orphaned or no-longer-trusted attestations. With consumer verification deletion may block use, and external artifact deletion can trigger cleanup automation. These destructive lifecycle proposals require authorization and recovery review; no attestations deleted.
macOS larger runners cannot join a network-configured group, and groups containing them cannot receive a network configuration. Constraint applies both association directions, not all runner types.
